skill_tags: Finding Areas of Composite Circular Regions

hints: Set up the area of the shaded region as $\frac{1}{2}(15^2)(\frac{2\pi}{5}) - \frac{1}{2}x^2(\frac{2\pi}{5}) = \frac{209\pi}{5}$.
Calculate the perimeter by summing the two straight edges $2(15 - 4)$ and the two curved arcs $15(\frac{2\pi}{5}) + 4(\frac{2\pi}{5})$.
walkthrough:
Use the sector area difference formula to find the inner radius $x$:
$$\text{Shaded Area} = \frac{1}{2}(15^2)\left(\frac{2\pi}{5}\right) - \frac{1}{2}x^2\left(\frac{2\pi}{5}\right) = \frac{209\pi}{5}$$
$$\frac{\pi}{5}(225 - x^2) = \frac{209\pi}{5} \implies 225 - x^2 = 209 \implies x^2 = 16 \implies x = 4\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the lengths of the two straight boundary edges $AB$ and $CD$:
$$AB = CD = 15 - 4 = 11\text{ cm} \implies AB + CD = 22\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the lengths of the two curved arcs $BC$ and $AD$:
$$\text{Arc } BC = r_1\theta = 15 \times \frac{2\pi}{5} = 6\pi\text{ cm}$$
$$\text{Arc } AD = r_2\theta = 4 \times \frac{2\pi}{5} = \frac{8\pi}{5}\text{ cm}$$

Sum all boundary parts to find the exact perimeter:
$$\text{Perimeter} = 22 + 6\pi + \frac{8\pi}{5} = 22 + \frac{38\pi}{5}\text{ cm}$$

ai_rubric.Calculating Perimeters: Sets up sector area difference to find $x = 4$ (M1, A1). Uses arc length formula for both arcs (M1). Obtains exact perimeter $22 + \frac{38}{5}\pi$ (A1).
